page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family, it provides 16 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core. This dedicated single-threaded topology mitigates resource contention common in simultaneous multithreading environments. Memory capacity is allocated at 32.0 GB total, establishing an exact 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent from this server configuration, and it contains no bundled local storage disks. Operating systems and user data require external network block storage for persistence. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource profile emphasizes dedicated core throughput over memory density, offering qualitative cost efficiency for organizations deploying scale-out ARM workloads without paying for unused memory allocations.

The primary tradeoff of VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-32 is the lack of local NVMe storage and relatively tight 2.0 GB per-core memory capacity, which limits suitability for memory-heavy databases or caching layers. It is best aligned with compute-bound workloads, such as ARM64 software compilation, continuous integration build nodes, containerized microservice execution, and scalable web serving tiers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-32 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on 64-bit ARM architecture using the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores mapped directly to 16 vCPUs with one thread per core, avoiding noisy-neighbor and hyperthreading contention. The system includes 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote cloud block storage for persistent data, and does not contain GPU hardware accelerators. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated core architecture and lean memory allocation, this instance delivers strong qualitative compute efficiency for CPU-bound, scale-out environments. VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.8-32 is appropriate for ARM-native application compilation, CI/CD build workers, distributed container services, batch processing, and horizontally scalable web application serving.
